title: Towards Professional-Grade Financial Agents: Benchmarking, Tooling, and Structured Reasoning
one_liner: ProFinAgent tackles finance work with a large task benchmark, a finance-specific tool library, and a directed acyclic plan, so that tool calls can run in the right order and in parallel when possible.
lead: Finance tasks often require several linked calculations, document lookups, and rule checks. A plain step-by-step agent can fail because it chooses tools in the wrong order, forgets past similar cases, or waits for one tool call to finish before starting independent work. ProFinR and ProFinAgent attack the problem at three levels. The benchmark defines what serious financial reasoning looks like. The Financial Tool Universe supplies domain-specific tools. The agent then plans work as a directed acyclic graph and consults a case memory of past examples. This structure improves both answer quality and speed because independent subproblems can run in parallel and past cases can guide choices early.

problem.h2: Why finance agents need more structure
paras: A professional finance task is rarely one isolated question. It may involve pulling market data, computing ratios, reading policy rules, comparing scenarios, and merging several intermediate results into one decision.

A loosely organized agent can break in two ways. It may reason with the wrong tool order because one calculation depends on another. It may also waste time by handling every subtask strictly one after another even when some parts are independent. The paper asks how to benchmark this setting and how to build an agent that respects both dependency structure and past experience.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Define a professional finance benchmark, supply a finance-specific tool universe, and plan tool usage as a directed acyclic graph with case memory, so that complex tasks can be solved with the right dependencies and faster execution.

paras: The paper changes financial agent work from unstructured sequential tool use to benchmarked domain-specific planning with explicit dependencies and reusable earlier cases.

hidden.name: how well the plan matches the true prerequisite structure of the financial task
paras: The key quantity is dependency fidelity. A financial answer is often wrong because one branch used inputs that had not been established yet or because two independent branches were handled as if one depended on the other.

ProFinAgent improves dependency fidelity with the directed acyclic plan and case memory. That helps accuracy because each tool call gets the information it actually needs, and it helps speed because independent branches can run together.

heat.caption: Dark cells mark plans that respect true task dependencies, because accurate ordering and parallelism improve both correctness and speed.

reads.html: The agent works better because it knows which subtask must happen first and which subtasks can happen at the same time.
ProFinAgent improves professional finance reasoning by planning tool usage with explicit dependency structure and by reusing similar past cases.

paras: The benchmark matters because professional finance reasoning is broader than a few isolated examples. A benchmark with many expert-designed problems forces the system to handle varied workflows rather than one narrow pattern.

The finance tool universe matters because domain tasks depend on calculations, lookups, and rules that a generic agent may not execute precisely on its own. Better tools improve the raw ingredients of the answer by producing more accurate intermediate results.

The directed acyclic plan is the central design choice because it captures both ordering and parallel opportunity. Case memory helps by supplying useful decompositions from similar tasks, so the planner starts from a stronger structure.

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: A task asks for a risk assessment that depends on current prices, company filings, and a ratio calculation.
Fetching prices and filings can happen together because they are independent branches.
The ratio calculation must wait because it needs the fetched numbers first.
A sequential agent waits too long and may mix the order, while the graph planner starts both fetches early and merges them only after both finish.
That improves both answer quality and speed because the plan respects the true dependency structure.

math.note: The objective summarizes the paper's main idea: good finance reasoning needs the right tools in the right order, because order errors damage both correctness and efficiency.

items.b: The dependency graph may be wrong.
items.html: If the planner misses a prerequisite edge, a later tool can run on incomplete data because the true task order was not captured.

items.b: Case memory may pull a misleading example.
items.html: A weak earlier case can bias the plan toward the wrong decomposition because the current task only looks similar on the surface.

items.b: The tool universe may still miss key operations.
items.html: A planner cannot fix a missing capability because some finance tasks need domain operations that generic tools do not provide.
The approach works when the graph matches real dependencies and the retrieved case is genuinely relevant, because then parallel branches and ordered merges both help.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small finance benchmark with tasks that require at least three kinds of subtasks, such as data lookup, document reading, and numerical calculation. Compare a strictly sequential tool agent with a graph planner that can run independent branches together and can reuse a small library of solved examples.
The demo should show higher answer quality and lower task time for the graph planner because it respects prerequisites and avoids waiting on branches that do not depend on each other.
demo.metric_eq: task_success = correct_finance_answers / total_tasks; branch_parallel_gain = sequential_time / graph_time
demo.closing: The decisive evidence is that structured graph planning improves both accuracy and speed, because professional finance tasks contain real dependency structure that sequential tool use wastes.
